claim: A table edit or a pack's patch can delete a row that items 122 and 123 read, and no fallback is defined. - **Why the delete goes through.** V11 §4.1 (l.4808-4814) refuses a delete in only four cases: a `defaultRow`, an `allowFallback` target, a `TotalityRule`'s only cover, or a non-`mayEmpty` table's last row. `crisis.looks` (registry row 107) and `damage.elements` (row 109) declare no `defaultRow`; V11 §2.1's list (l.287-289) names none for them. They declare no `TotalityRule` either: `coversEnum` appears only in the interface (l.277). Their "one row per `CrisisLookKind`" and "one row per `DamageElementKind`" are compile checks of the shipped rows (T-V11-46 (b), T-V11-47 (a)), not rules a document's `editTable` meets. - **What follows.** A delete of `crisis.looks`' `siege` row, of `damage.elements`' `roofBay` row, or of either table's named `settings` row is accepted. Then: - DR44 maps a standing siege condition through its `crisis.map` row to a look kind that has no row; - §6.3's threshold t = lo + u · (hi − lo) has no [lo, hi] for any roof bay; - `densityCap`, `previewSeverity`, `areaPerHeadM2`, `enginesPerBesiegers` or `defaultAgeYears` has no value. - **Why no fallback covers it.** V11 §3.26's general rule (l.4711-4714) sends a reader that meets an absent row to the table's `defaultRow` or to "the row's neutral value (V11 §3.2.3 (c)–(d))". §3.2.3 (d) defines a neutral value only for a derived family row. - **What the text already covers.** §2.9's `crises` key covers only a `preview` whose look is "gone after a table edit". Neither DR44's `follow` path nor a damage element is covered, and EI-V11-EDGE-4 and -5 do not list the delete.
required_change: 1. **The totality rules.** V11 §2.1's registry gives row 107 (`crisis.looks`) `totality: [{ kind: 'coversEnum', column: 'kind', of: 'CrisisLookKind' }]` and row 109 (`damage.elements`) `totality: [{ kind: 'coversEnum', column: 'kind', of: 'DamageElementKind' }]`. T-V11-46 (b)'s and T-V11-47 (a)'s one-row-per-kind clauses are then these rules' compile form. 2. **V11 §4.1's required-row sentence** adds "or of a table's named row (`settings`, `structure`; V11 §2.1's settings form)". A delete of a look kind's row, an element kind's row or either table's `settings` row — by `editTable` or a pack's patch — is then refused with `refuse.table.required`. The refusal names the readers and offers "edit its cells": - for `crisis.looks`: DR44, §10.2 and §8.2's look rows; - for `damage.elements`: §6.3's thresholds, V06 §3.23, V03, V02 and V04. 3. **The edge rows.** EI-V11-EDGE-4 and EI-V11-EDGE-5 each add "a delete of a kind's row or of the `settings` row" with that outcome. 4. **The test.** T-V11-45 (s) adds three tables-editor deletes: `crisis.looks`' `siege` row, `damage.elements`' `roofBay` row and `crisis.looks`' `settings` row. Each is refused and the tables are unchanged.

claim: §4.7's new step regions (l. 6743–6745) split a step above `stepMaxCm` into ⌈step ÷ `stepMaxCm`⌉ equal parts, 'so every wall on the line retains more than `stepMaxCm` ÷ 2 and at most `stepMaxCm`'. §4.7 (l. 6731–6732) and V11 (l. 3858) also say a step below `terrace.stepMinCm` is never a wall (the plinth). T-V11-32 (a) (l. 3855) bounds only `plinthCm < stepMinCm < skirtMaxCm < stepMaxCm`. A lawful edited row therefore yields an intermediate wall retaining less than `stepMinCm`: the base's `skirtMaxCm` is 300 cm and `stepMaxCm` 400, so `stepMinCm` 250 passes, and a 450 cm step splits into two 225 cm walls. That contradicts the stepMinCm rule, and EP-24's bar (every wall's `stepProfile` in (`stepMinCm`, `stepMaxCm`]) fails. The pipeline repair handed V11 the guard; it was not applied.
required_change: V11 T-V11-32 (a), l. 3855: add '`stepMinCm` < `stepMaxCm` ÷ 2 (so every intermediate wall of §4.7's step regions, more than `stepMaxCm` ÷ 2, is a wall)'. The tables editor's clamp (l. 3860) and V11 §3.24.1's range column then hold it.

claim: The crisis census has two names and two totality scopes. V08 §2.4 declares the catalogue manifest's census as `crisis: { stressors; archetypes; events }`, and V08 §3.16 (7) (a) says V11's compile check makes 'every census word' have its row. T-V11-46 (a) and V11 §3.25.9's *Totality* check 'the catalogue manifest's `sf.stressors@<line>` list' and 'its `sf.conditionArchetypes@<line>` list' — names V08 never declares — and do not check the `events` list. The `event` rows (`PLAGUE`, `REFUGEE_WAVE`, `RAID_OR_MONSTER_ATTACK`) are therefore never proven total against the census.
required_change: T-V11-46 (a) and V11 §3.25.9's *Totality*: 'the catalogue manifest's `sf.stressors@<line>` list' → 'the catalogue manifest's `crisis.stressors` list (V08 §2.4)'; '`sf.conditionArchetypes@<line>` list' → '`crisis.archetypes` list'; add 'and every word of its `crisis.events` list its `event` row'. Registry row 77's reader column adds 'the `crisis.map` compile check (T-V11-46 (a))'.

claim: V11 §3.25.11 gives each weather kind `hours` — "the hours of the view's day a spell may start in, read only under `light: 'time'` (§2.9), so fog and mist come on cool mornings" (`mist` and `fog` 4–11, `shimmer` 10–18) — but its timeline rule reads "At a week the kinds whose band holds it are live, each at its `perHour` × the largest factor of the sites …; with R their sum, the clear time after a spell (and from the map's opening) is exponential with mean 3 600 ÷ R s, the next kind is k with chance perHour_k ÷ R". `hours` enters neither R nor the kind's chance, so when a gap ends at a view hour outside the drawn kind's hours (fog drawn at 14:00 under `light: 'time'`) the spell "may" not start and nothing says whether it is dropped, deferred to the next admitted hour or redrawn; EI-V11-EDGE-6 covers only "a `light` other than `'time'`". The base end is verify-determinism-r2t's VDC2-01 (§6.1 *The weather stream*: liveness including the kinds' `hours`, the gap spent at the live rate); V11's own rule must say the same (R2-05).
required_change: In V11 §3.25.11's *The columns* bullet replace "At a week the kinds whose band holds it are live, each at its `perHour` × the largest factor of the sites that apply (below); with R their sum, the clear time after a spell (and from the map's opening) is exponential with mean 3 600 ÷ R s, the next kind is k with chance perHour_k ÷ R" with "At a moment the kinds whose band holds the view's week and — under `light: 'time'` — whose `hours` hold the view's hour are live, each at its `perHour` × the largest factor of the sites that apply (below); with R their sum, the clear time after a spell (and from the map's opening) is spent at that live rate (§6.1: a unit exponential spent as the integral of R ÷ 3 600 over view time, none spent while R is 0), and the next kind is k with chance perHour_k ÷ R at the moment the gap ends". In *The kinds*' head, "`hours` the hours of the view's day a spell may start in" → "`hours` the hours of the view's day in which the kind is live". EI-V11-EDGE-6 adds the case "a kind whose `hours` exclude the view's hour" with the outcome "not live then: it adds nothing to R and is never drawn at that hour", and T-V11-45 (v) adds that fixture.
